# 2 Maccabees Chapter 9 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 9 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_009_page_001.jpg

---

**9:1** Now about that time it happened that Antiochus retreated in disorder from the regions of Persia.

**9:2** For he had entered into the city called Persepolis and attempted to plunder the temple and to control the city. Thereupon the multitudes rushed to arms for defense, and it came about that Antiochus was put to flight by the inhabitants and withdrew with disgrace.

**9:3** And while he was in Ecbatana, news was brought to him concerning what had happened to Nicanor and the forces of Timothy.

**9:4** And being lifted up in passion he thought to make the Jews suffer for the injury done by those who had put him to flight. Therefore he commanded his charioteer to drive without stopping until he should complete the journey. But the judgment of heaven accompanied him, for he had said in his arrogance, "I will make Jerusalem a common graveyard of Jews when I arrive there."

**9:5** But the all-seeing Lord, the God of Israel, struck him with a blow that was invisible and incurable. For as soon as he had spoken this word, an irremediable pain in his bowels seized him and bitter torments of the inner parts.

**9:6** And indeed very justly, for he had tormented the bowels of others with many and strange inflictions.

**9:7** Yet he did not at all cease from his arrogance; rather he was still more filled with pride. Breathing fire in his passion against the Jews, he gave orders to hasten the journey. But it came about that he fell from the chariot as it was rushing along, and was rolled violently so that every member of his body was racked by the fall.

**9:8** Thus he who in his superhuman arrogance had thought to command the waves of the sea and to weigh the high mountains on a scale was now brought down to the ground and carried in a litter, making the power of God manifest to all.

**9:9** And worms swarmed out of the body of this impious man, and while he was still living in anguish and pain, his flesh fell off, and because of the stench the whole army was revolted by the decay.

**9:10** And the man who a little while before had thought he could touch the stars of heaven, no one was able to carry because of the unbearable stench.

**9:11** Then it was that, broken in spirit, he began to come out of his great arrogance, and to come to knowledge under the lash of God, since he was racked with pain every moment.

**9:12** And when he could not endure his own stench, he said this: "It is right to be subject to God, and one who is mortal should not think equal things with God."

**9:13** And the vile man vowed to the Lord, who would no longer have mercy on him, as follows:

**9:14** that the holy city, to which he was hastening to level it to the ground and to make it a common graveyard, he would declare free;

**9:15** and the Jews, whom he had decided not even to count worthy of burial but to give to the birds and the wild animals, together with their infant children, he would make equal to the citizens of Athens;

**9:16** and the holy sanctuary, which he had formerly plundered, he would adorn with the finest offerings; and the sacred vessels he would restore many times over; and the expenses required for the sacrifices he would provide from his own revenues;

**9:17** and in addition to all this he would also become a Jew and would go through every inhabited place proclaiming the power of God.

**9:18** But when his sufferings did not in any way cease, for the judgment of God had come upon him justly, having given up hope about himself, he wrote to the Jews the letter written below, in the character of a supplication. It ran as follows:

**9:19** "To the worthy Jewish citizens, Antiochus the king and general sends many greetings and hopes for health and welfare.

**9:20** If you and your children are well and your affairs are as you wish, I give very great thanks to God, having my hope in heaven.

**9:21** I am also laid low in body, but yet remembering with affection the honor and goodwill toward you, returning from the regions of Persia and being struck by a troublesome illness, I considered it necessary to take care for the general safety of all.

**9:22** Not despairing of my condition — for I have good hope of recovering from the illness —

**9:23** but considering that my father also, at the times when he led campaigns into the upper regions, appointed his successor,

**9:24** so that if anything unexpected happened or any difficult news came, those throughout the land, knowing to whom the affairs had been left, might not be troubled,

**9:25** and observing besides that the neighboring princes, who are neighbors of my kingdom, are watchful and expecting the occasion — I have designated my son Antiochus to be king, whom I have often committed to most of you when I traveled at speed into the upper provinces. I have written to him what I have written below.

**9:26** I therefore exhort and beg you to remember the public and private benefits and to preserve each his goodwill toward me and my son.

**9:27** For I am confident that he will be moderate and kind and will follow my policy in being gracious toward you."

**9:28** Thus the murderer and blasphemer, having endured the most intense suffering, as he had made others suffer, ended his life in a most pitiable manner among the mountains in a strange land.

**9:29** And Philip, his foster brother, took the body back. Then, fearing the son of Antiochus, he withdrew to Ptolemy Philometor in Egypt.
